rule: A planet is exalted (uchcha) in one fixed sign: Sun in Mesha, Moon in Vrishabha, Mars in Makara, Mercury in Kanya, Jupiter in Karka, Venus in Meena, Saturn in Tula.
text: The exalted tag means this planet sits in the one sign Parashara names as its exaltation: Sun in Mesha, Moon in Vrishabha, Mars in Makara, Mercury in Kanya, Jupiter in Karka, Venus in Meena, Saturn in Tula. It was determined from the planet's sidereal sign alone, not its degree. Classically the planet's qualities are read as expressed with full confidence and ease, so the sign and house readings tend to apply strongly. Rahu and Ketu carry no exaltation tag in this app.

rule: A planet is debilitated (neecha) in the sign opposite its exaltation: Sun in Tula, Moon in Vrishchika, Mars in Karka, Mercury in Meena, Jupiter in Makara, Venus in Kanya, Saturn in Mesha.
text: The debilitated tag means this planet sits in the sign opposite its exaltation: Sun in Tula, Moon in Vrishchika, Mars in Karka, Mercury in Meena, Jupiter in Makara, Venus in Kanya, Saturn in Mesha. It was determined from the sidereal sign alone. Classically the planet's natural style is read as working against the grain of the sign, so its themes tend to need more conscious effort and often develop in unusual ways. The tag describes a tendency, not a verdict; cancellation rules (neecha bhanga) are not applied here.

rule: A planet is in its own sign (swakshetra) when it rules the sign it occupies; moolatrikona is folded into this tag.
text: The own sign tag means this planet occupies a sign it rules: Sun in Simha, Moon in Karka, Mars in Mesha or Vrishchika, Mercury in Mithuna, Jupiter in Dhanu or Meena, Venus in Vrishabha or Tula, Saturn in Makara or Kumbha. It was determined from the sign lord table. Classically a planet at home is read as steady and self-possessed, expressing its nature without strain. Moolatrikona, the planet's preferred degrees within its own sign, is folded into this one tag in this app.

rule: A planet is in a friend's sign when the sign's lord is its natural friend in Parashara's table of friendships.
text: The friend's sign tag means the lord of the sign this planet occupies is its natural friend in Parashara's table of permanent (naisargika) friendships: for example the Sun counts Moon, Mars and Jupiter as friends, and Venus counts Mercury and Saturn. It was determined by looking up the sign's lord and reading the planet's row in that table. Classically a planet among friends is read as supported, so its qualities tend to come through comfortably. Temporary friendships based on the chart are not used here.

rule: A planet is in an enemy's sign when the sign's lord is its natural enemy in Parashara's table of friendships.
text: The enemy sign tag means the lord of the sign this planet occupies is its natural enemy in Parashara's table of permanent friendships: for example the Sun counts Venus and Saturn as enemies, and Saturn counts Sun, Moon and Mars. It was determined from the sign's lord and the planet's row in that table. Classically a planet in an enemy's house is read as working in unfamiliar territory, so its themes tend to take more negotiation. The tag describes a tendency and does not override the rest of the chart.

rule: A planet is in a neutral sign when the sign's lord is neither friend nor enemy in Parashara's table of friendships.
text: The neutral tag means the lord of the sign this planet occupies is neither friend nor enemy in Parashara's table of permanent friendships; for example the Moon is neutral toward Mars, Jupiter, Venus and Saturn. It was determined from the sign's lord and the planet's row in that table. Classically a planet in neutral ground is read as neither helped nor hindered by the sign, so the sign and house readings apply in their plain form. Rahu and Ketu receive no relationship tag in this app.

rule: A planet is combust (asta) when it lies within its orb of the Sun: Moon 12°, Mars 17°, Mercury 14° (12° retrograde), Jupiter 11°, Venus 10° (8° retrograde), Saturn 15°.
text: The combust tag means this planet lies within its combustion orb of the Sun, measured along the ecliptic: Moon 12°, Mars 17°, Mercury 14° (12° when retrograde), Jupiter 11°, Venus 10° (8° when retrograde), Saturn 15°. Rahu and Ketu are never marked combust. The distance and orb used are listed under How this was computed. Classically a combust planet is read as outshone by the Sun, so its themes tend to be absorbed into questions of identity and expressed less independently. It is a tendency, not a disqualification.

rule: A planet is retrograde (vakri) when its longitude decreases from day to day as seen from Earth; the Sun and Moon never are, Rahu and Ketu almost always are.
text: The retrograde tag means this planet's sidereal longitude was decreasing at the birth moment, so it appeared to move backward against the stars as seen from Earth; the daily speed is shown with the tag. The Sun and Moon are never retrograde. Rahu and Ketu move backward by construction, so no tag is shown for them. Classically a retrograde planet is read as turning its themes inward or revisiting them, so the sign and house readings tend to apply in a reflective, second-look manner.

rule: A planet is vargottama when it occupies the same sign in the D1 Rashi chart and the D9 Navamsa.
text: The vargottama tag means this planet occupies the same sign in the birth chart (D1) and in the ninth division, the Navamsa (D9). That happens in the first navamsa of a movable sign, the fifth of a fixed sign and the ninth of a dual sign, each navamsa spanning 3°20'. It was determined by computing both signs from the sidereal longitude. Classically a vargottama planet is read as consistent, its sign themes reinforced rather than diluted, so the sign reading tends to apply with extra steadiness.

rule: The Lagna carries approx. when the birth time was entered as approximate and shifting it by the stated minutes moves the rising sign, or when the Lagna lies within 1° of a sign boundary.
text: The approx. tag on the Lagna means the rising sign cannot be stated with confidence from the inputs given. It appears when the Lagna lies within 1° of a sign boundary, or when the birth time was entered as approximate and shifting it by the stated window (15, 30 or 60 minutes) would move the Lagna into another sign. Because the Lagna changes sign roughly every two hours, a few minutes can matter. Every house, house lord and Lagna reading then inherits this uncertainty and is read with that caution.

rule: A planet carries approx. when it lies within 1° of a sign boundary, or when the declared birth-time window moves it across one.
text: The approx. tag on a planet means its sign cannot be stated with confidence. It appears when the planet lies within 1° of a sign boundary, where small differences in ayanamsa or recorded time would change the sign, or when the birth time was entered as approximate and the planet crosses a boundary within that window. The Moon moves about 13° a day and is the most affected; slow planets rarely qualify. The sign, house and dignity readings for this planet are read as provisional.

rule: With the birth time unknown the Lagna cannot be computed, so the Moon sign is placed in house 1 and houses are counted from it; dashas stay valid because they depend only on the Moon.
text: Moon chart mode means the birth time was marked unknown, so the Lagna, which depends on the exact time and place, could not be computed. Planet positions were taken at local noon with a twelve-hour window on either side, the Moon's sign was placed in house 1 and the other houses were counted from it. Readings that depend on the Lagna, such as house lords and Chalit, are hidden. Dashas remain valid because they depend only on the Moon's position, which the window usually leaves within one nakshatra.

rule: In whole-sign houses each house is one full sign counted from the Lagna, and its lord is the ruler of that sign.
text: The house lord shown for each house is the planet that rules the sign occupying that house. This app uses whole-sign houses: house 1 is the entire Lagna sign, house 2 the next sign, and so on, so each house has exactly one sign and one lord. The lords follow the fixed rulerships listed under sign lord (Mars for Mesha and Vrishchika, Venus for Vrishabha and Tula, and so on). The lord's own sign and house are read for how that house's themes are carried.

rule: Each sign has a fixed ruling planet: Mars (Mesha, Vrishchika), Venus (Vrishabha, Tula), Mercury (Mithuna, Kanya), Moon (Karka), Sun (Simha), Jupiter (Dhanu, Meena), Saturn (Makara, Kumbha).
text: The sign lord named in a planet-in-sign reading is the fixed ruler of that sign in the classical scheme: Mars rules Mesha and Vrishchika, Venus rules Vrishabha and Tula, Mercury rules Mithuna and Kanya, the Moon rules Karka, the Sun rules Simha, Jupiter rules Dhanu and Meena, Saturn rules Makara and Kumbha. Rahu and Ketu rule no sign. The lord is what links a planet to its dignity tag: the relationship between the planet and the sign's lord decides whether the sign counts as a friend's, an enemy's or neutral.
